raw_case_text: A 53-year-old woman with no significant underlying medical history was admitted to our hospital with a 1-month history of intermittent fever. She ever picked Zanthoxylum seeds in Hancheng, China 8 years ago, and she had a history of mosquito bites. She had a history of esophageal cancer and received surgical treatment one and a half years ago, and there was no recurrence after operation. Past medical, past surgical, drug and family histories were not significant. Her body weight was 55 kg. Physical examination revealed splenomegaly and axillary and inguinal lymphadenopathy. Laboratory tests revealed high levels of CRP (97.3 mg/L; reference value, <10.0 mg/L), as well as elevated liver enzyme levels, abnormal coagulation, and pancytopenia. Her PCT level was 1.24 ng/mL. Antibodies against Leishmania were detected in her blood. A positive PCR result for Leishmania in bone marrow aspirate confirmed the diagnosis of VL. She received prompt treatment with L-AmB at an initial dose of 5 mg (~0.10 mg/kg) on the first day. The L-AmB protocol for the patient is presented in Figure 3. During L-AmB dose escalation, laboratory tests of renal functions and electrolytes uncovered no particular abnormality during treatment. Routine blood parameters gradually normalized during therapy, and her spleen size gradually decreased. No VL recurrence was observed at the 1-year follow-up visit.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 53-year-old woman presented with a 1-month history of intermittent fever.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient developed intermittent fevers lasting 1 month prior to hospital admission.
subjective.past_medical_history: History of esophageal cancer surgically resected 1.5 years earlier without recurrence; history of picking Zanthoxylum (Sichuan pepper) seeds in Hancheng, Shaanxi Province, China (a visceral leishmaniasis-endemic area) 8 years earlier with recalled insect/mosquito bites.

objective.physical_examination: Body weight 55 kg; febrile with splenomegaly and palpable axillary and inguinal lymphadenopathy.
objective.routine_investigations: Labs showed pancytopenia, elevated hepatic transaminases, abnormal coagulation profile, CRP 97.3 mg/L (ref <10.0 mg/L), procalcitonin 1.24 ng/mL, and positive serum anti-Leishmania antibodies.
objective.advanced_workup: Bone marrow aspirate PCR was positive for Leishmania.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Positive peripheral blood anti-Leishmania antibodies and positive bone marrow aspirate Leishmania PCR confirmed Visceral Leishmaniasis. Treatment with a low-dose escalating regimen of intravenous liposomal amphotericin B (starting at 5 mg [~0.10 mg/kg] on day 1) was completed without renal or electrolyte toxicity, achieving gradual normalization of blood counts, regression of splenomegaly, and relapse-free survival at 1-year follow-up.
